intro: A document classifier can learn class-specific token frequencies from count vectors. Additive smoothing keeps unseen vocabulary entries usable.
task: Fit empirical class priors and smoothed multinomial feature probabilities from labeled count vectors.
requirements: counts is a nonnegative integer-valued (n,d) matrix. labels contains n integer-valued class IDs. classes is an integer in [1,128], and every class must occur.
alpha is a scalar in [1e-8,1e6]. Sum feature counts within each class, add alpha to every feature, and normalize by total counts plus alpha*d.
Return {"class_log_prior": log(class_row_counts/n), "feature_log_probability": log(smoothed_probabilities)}. Class priors are not smoothed; token-empty rows still count toward them.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Two document classes
Empty document
Unequal class prior

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Observation counts set class priors, whereas token counts within a class set feature probabilities.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Apply smoothing to every vocabulary entry before computing the row denominator, including unseen entries.

explanation: Feature counts are accumulated within each class rather than averaged per document. Additive smoothing distributes a fixed pseudo-count across the vocabulary before normalization.
Class prior counts observations, whereas feature likelihood counts tokens. Treating those as the same denominator would change the model when document lengths differ.
